Subject: PO template + invoice cadence requirements

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — product looks promising. Procurement has a few standard requirements we need to confirm before we can issue a Master PO:

- Our finance policy requires Net60 payment terms for new vendors unless there is an approved prepayment exception.
- Invoices must include: Customer PO number, Lumina legal entity (Lumina Health, Inc.), Bill-to and Ship-to entity codes, Tax ID, and a remittance address.
- We prefer consolidated monthly invoices per legal entity; however, for shared services across entities we can accept a single invoice with line-item entity mapping.

I attached our PO template (Lumina_PO_template_v2.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood can populate the required header fields and accept Net60? Also, please highlight any impact on pricing/discounts if we cannot prepay or move to Net30.

Sophie Hart
Senior Procurement Manager
Lumina Health

Hi Sophie — thanks for the template and the clear list. Quick answers up front:

- Yes, we can include the PO number, legal entity, billing codes and Tax ID on each invoice.
- We can support either consolidated monthly invoices per legal entity or single invoices with line-item entity mapping; we will need the mapping CSV (entity -> BU code) on Go-Live.
- Net60 is not our default for enterprise because of receivable exposure, but we can discuss an exception. There are a few paths:
  * Keep list pricing but accept Net60 (carrier-level exception)
  * Apply a small pricing uplift to compensate for extended terms (we typically model a ~1.75-2.5% uplift for Net60 vs Net30 depending on commitment length)
  * Maintain discount tiers tied to committed ARR or prepayment (annual prepay = strongest discount)

I've attached our Redwood-pricing-proposal-2026.xlsx with three packaging options: subscription annual prepay, quarterly invoices with 3% discount, and monthly invoices with Net60 + small uplift.

Next steps I propose: 1) Lumina confirms billing entities and whether multi-entity line mapping is acceptable; 2) Procurement confirms Net60 is firm and whether prepay is possible for partial upfront; 3) If Net60 is required and prepay is not possible, we schedule a short call to review uplift scenarios and agree on a final term.

Can Karthik and Ben weigh in on the discount tradeoffs below?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie — Ben here from sales. Appreciate the clarity. A few operational notes and a couple proposal options to simplify approvals on both sides:

Operational checklist (what we need on the PO):
- PO number, legal entity name, billing entity code, Tax ID/EIN, remittance address, currency (USD), and the billing contact name/email.
- If multiple Lumina entities are being billed, please indicate primary payer (entity responsible for payment) and specify whether you want separate invoices or a single consolidated invoice with entity line-mapping.

Commercial options:
1) Quarterly invoicing (invoice at start of quarter) + 3% discount off list 
   - No prepay required; finance friendly; we can issue consolidated quarterly invoice split by entity when line mapping provided.
2) Monthly invoicing with Net60 + 1.9% netterm uplift 
   - Slight price premium to cover extended receivable exposure; we can include automatic invoice reminders but would need a credit request form signed.
3) Annual prepay = 6.5% discount (best economics)

If Lumina cannot accept prepay and Net60 is non-negotiable, option 2 is likely the cleanest path — keeps the contract simple and preserves some discount through an uplift. We're happy to draft language clarifying invoice format so your AP team can match it in ERP.

Can you share a sample completed PO so we can do a dry run through our billing system?

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Vanessa / Ben — quick internal update: our policy team confirmed that Net60 is the baseline for our onboarding of new vendors. Prepay is only allowed with CFO sign-off and business case. We cannot move to Net30.

A few clarifications from finance:
- They will accept consolidated monthly invoices only if each invoice includes a CSV line mapping file that our ERP can ingest (we can provide the spec).
- We have three legal entities in scope for this purchase; we will not provide a single payer for the full amount. Each entity must be reflected on invoices.
- On discounts: procurement can request an exception to allow a deeper discount but that requires a formal approval route (procurement -> finance -> CFO) and a business case showing expected cost savings vs. cashflow impact.

Attaching our finance policy excerpt (lumina-finance-policy-2026.pdf). Can Redwood provide the CSV mapping template and confirm you can generate per-invoice CSV exports automatically? Also need confirmation on whether the uplift pricing for Net60 is fixed or negotiable based on committed ARR.

Thanks,
Sophie

- If Net60 is required and prepay is not available, we propose a modest uplift (we suggest 1.9% as a starting point) to offset receivable risk; uplift is negotiable against committed ARR bands.

2) Redwood will send a short sample invoice + corresponding CSV mapping to validate with Lumina ERP by Wed 2/18.

4) Final PO execution target: Fri 2/27 (subject to CFO approval window).

If that timeline works I will book a 30-minute alignment call for Tue 2/17 at 10:00 PT to walk through the sample invoice and mapping.
